summary: This lecture tells what happened after the first revelation at Hira. The ustaz mentions Usamah ibn Zaid, the young commander of the Prophet's last expedition, then repeats the first five verses of Al-Alaq. The Prophet SAW ran home frightened and worried he was possessed, and Khadijah covered and calmed him by naming his good deeds: keeping family ties, honouring guests and helping the poor. Khadijah took him to her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal, who read the earlier scriptures, recognised Jibril as An-Namus and said he would be driven out by his people. The ustaz then lists the first believers: Khadijah, Waraqah, Ali, Abu Bakr and Fatimah bint Asad, and how prayer was at first twice a day.
keyPoints: The Prophet SAW ran home frightened and asked to be covered, worried he was possessed.
Khadijah calmed him by naming his good deeds: keeping family ties, honouring guests and helping the poor.
Waraqah ibn Nawfal recognised Jibril as An-Namus and said his people would drive him out.
Khadijah, Ali, Abu Bakr and Fatimah bint Asad were among the earliest to believe.
At first prayer was only twice a day, dawn and sunset, until the five prayers were prescribed later.

chapters.title: Opening
chapters.summary: The ustaz gives thanks, mentions world news and a prayer for Gaza before continuing the sirah.

chapters.title: Usamah ibn Zaid
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW appointed Usamah, son of Zaid and Ummu Aiman called the beloved of the Messenger, as leader of the last expedition at 16.

chapters.title: The first revelation revisited
chapters.summary: The ustaz repeats the first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq and the embrace by Jibril.

chapters.title: Running home in fear
chapters.summary: He descended Jabal Nur and ran home, afraid of being possessed by a jinn, and asked Khadijah to cover him.

chapters.title: Khadijah calms him
chapters.summary: Khadijah said Allah would never disgrace him because he kept family ties, honoured guests and helped the poor.

chapters.title: Khadijah takes him to Waraqah
chapters.summary: Waraqah ibn Nawfal was Khadijah's elderly, blind cousin, an expert in the Torah and Gospel.

chapters.title: An-Namus
chapters.summary: The Prophet SAW told his experience and Waraqah said it was An-Namus, Jibril who came to Prophet Musa.

chapters.title: You will be driven out
chapters.summary: Waraqah wished to be young to help him when driven out, since every bearer of such a message is driven out by his people.

chapters.title: Waraqah dies and Surah Al-Qalam
chapters.summary: Waraqah kissed his head and then died. The second surah revealed was Al-Qalam, affirming his great character.

chapters.title: The first believers
chapters.summary: Khadijah was the first to believe and Waraqah counted as the first elderly man, and he dreamed of seeing him in paradise.

chapters.title: The household of the Prophet SAW
chapters.summary: The ustaz counts the residents of his house including the children, Zaid, Ummu Aiman and Ali taken from Abu Talib.

chapters.title: Ali sees the prayer
chapters.summary: Ali, aged six or seven, saw the Prophet SAW and Khadijah praying and asked.

chapters.title: Abu Talib and Ali
chapters.summary: Abu Talib told Ali to follow Muhammad but refused to leave the religion of Abdul Muttalib himself.

chapters.title: Abu Bakr believes at once
chapters.summary: Abu Bakr, named for a young camel, believed at once and brought his friends such as Uthman to Islam.

chapters.title: Prayer twice a day
chapters.summary: At first prayer was twice a day and Jibril taught wudu. The five prayers began ten years later.

chapters.title: Fatimah bint Asad and recap
chapters.summary: Fatimah bint Asad was among the earliest women to believe. The ustaz recaps and says the Prophet SAW was driven out 13 years later.

sirah.era: After the first revelation: the first days of the call
sirah.summary: This lecture tells the Prophet's reaction after the first revelation, Waraqah and the first to believe.

events.label: Return
events.title: The Prophet SAW runs home
events.desc: He descended Jabal Nur and asked Khadijah to cover him.

events.label: Waraqah
events.title: Meeting Waraqah
events.desc: Waraqah said this was An-Namus and that he would be driven out.

events.label: Death
events.title: Waraqah dies
events.desc: Waraqah kissed his head and died not long after.

events.label: Ali
events.title: Ali joins the prayer
events.desc: Ali saw him and Khadijah pray and joined them.

events.label: Abu Bakr
events.title: Abu Bakr believes
events.desc: Abu Bakr believed at once when told he had been appointed a messenger.

events.label: Prayer
events.title: Prayer twice a day
events.desc: Jibril taught wudu and prayer, twice a day at first.

lessons.title: A spouse who comforts
lessons.body: Khadijah comforted him with her confidence that Allah would not disgrace him.

lessons.title: Keeping family ties
lessons.body: Silaturahim is the bond with family who come from the same womb.

lessons.title: Honouring guests
lessons.body: Guests are treated specially for three days, and guests should realise when they stay too long.

lessons.title: Bearers of truth are often opposed
lessons.body: Everyone who brings a message like this is driven out by his people, as Waraqah said.

lessons.title: Great character
lessons.body: Allah affirms that he is of great character and not insane.

lessons.title: Asking parents' permission
lessons.body: Ali said he needed to ask Abu Talib before embracing Islam.

lessons.title: Believing because one knows honesty
lessons.body: Abu Bakr believed at once because he had known his friend's honesty since childhood.

lessons.title: Inviting friends to goodness
lessons.body: Abu Bakr promptly invited his good friends to join Islam.

lessons.title: Prayer began gradually
lessons.body: Prayer was at first twice a day before becoming five times.
